sources.title: Schedule or reschedule a Production Job
sources.guidance: Authorized business writers can stage Production schedules. Open a Job and enter both Planned start and Planned finish in Details, or adjust its bar in Timeline. Review changes, then choose Save all changes. Editing dates or releasing a Timeline drag stages the proposal without saving it. Finish must be on or after start. Save ordinary Inspector details first if prompted. Red scheduling errors block saving; warnings do not. Discard all restores the saved dates. A stale or failed save retains proposals for review rather than silently replacing them.
sources.path: Production → Job → Details → Planned start / Planned finish → Review changes → Save all changes

sources.title: Production Timeline and staged schedule
sources.guidance: Ordinary Production Timeline is available independently of disabled Phase/Item Planning. Staging does not save; approval and explicit confirmation are required. Read-only accounts may view but cannot stage changes. The proposed status bar remains editable, while a neutral dashed ghost identifies its last persisted position. A persistent control above the active view compares saved and proposed dates, days, and labor intensity and provides explicit Save and Discard actions. Table planned dates show the proposal with an unsaved indicator and feed changes into the same staged proposal. Table/Timeline switching and filtering preserve pending Production and Planning changes, while page navigation and browser unload are protected by confirmation. Labor intensity is derived rather than stored. Timeline ranges and their labor denominator both use inclusive calendar days: estimated labor hours divided by every scheduled calendar day. This interim model keeps scheduling honest about possible weekend work without implying that every included weekend is necessarily planned production time. A future shop calendar or job-specific planned-production-day model should replace it. Holiday calendars, workforce capacity, resource leveling, dependency scheduling, and automatic schedule optimization are deferred. Missing, zero, or invalid labor estimates are shown as No labor estimate rather than as zero labor. Static source interface text (labels do not establish a click sequence or additional permissions): Review proposed schedules · Close · Production changes · Revert this job · Planning changes · Revert this Phase · Scheduling feedback
sources.path: Production → Timeline → Save All / Discard All

sources.title: Find a Production Job
sources.guidance: Authorized operational readers can find the same Production Jobs in Overview, Table or Timeline. Open Production → Production Pipeline and use Search jobs. Search matches project name, customer, Job number, estimate number, work order, color plate and remarks. Select a Job to open its Inspector. Filters can restrict Scheduled/Unscheduled and Production Status; business writers can use Include Archived when looking for archived Jobs. Read-only accounts can search the current visible list. Search and filters change the displayed Jobs, not their saved records.
sources.path: Production → Production Pipeline → Search jobs → select a Job
